metadata.title: Can AI Discover New Quantum Materials?
metadata.color_semantics: PAGE #FAF9F5 ground; INK #3D3929 all text; ACCENT #D97757 terracotta on the one thing that matters per scene; SOFT #73705F secondary; BORDER #E5E2D9 card edges. One accent per beat.
metadata.audience: Technical generalists, research students, and practitioners reading AI-for-science headlines
framework_expansion: C — Composition: is there an exact, synthesizable formula?
L — Labels: was the model trained on measured Tc or a computed proxy?
A — Applicability: is the candidate inside the training distribution?
I — Independent confirmation: has another laboratory reproduced it?
M — Measurement: zero resistance AND the Meissner effect — at what pressure?

metadata.description_blurb: Can AI discover a new quantum material? This is an evidence-first review of what machine learning actually does in superconductor search — the public SuperCon-derived training table, the screening funnel, and the four physical steps a model never touches. Includes the LK-99 case as a worked falsifiability test and a reusable five-axis review scaffold you can run on any AI-materials headline.
metadata.disclaimer: Educational research review. No new superconductor is claimed, and no discovery campaign was performed for this film.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Dhrumil Shah. Can artificial intelligence discover a new quantum material? Here is the three-minute answer. AI does not discover superconductors. It reorders the search queue. The laboratory still decides.

shot.on_screen: Title, answer card, and the Search/Rank/Synthesize/Measure/Confirm pipeline as a VERTICAL stack with down-arrow connectors.
shot.source_tag: Presenter thesis · pipeline is this film's review structure

beats.narration_text: Superconductivity is a quantum effect you can measure. Below a critical temperature, electrons bind into pairs and current flows with exactly zero resistance. Raising that temperature has been the central problem since nineteen eleven.

shot.on_screen: Tc definition card full width, then an 860px-tall measured critical-temperature scatter. YBCO label left-anchored clear of the BSCCO point.
shot.source_tag: Kamerlingh Onnes 1911 · Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer 1957 · measured Tc record

beats.narration_text: So before any example, here is the frame I hold every claim to. Five questions. I call it CLAIM. It is my review structure, not a feature of any software.

shot.on_screen: Five CLAIM cards revealed as a 3+2 grid, explicitly labelled PRESENTER FRAMEWORK.
shot.source_tag: Presenter framework for this film · not a software feature

beats.narration_text: Start with what enters the model. The standard public training table comes from the SuperCon database, published by Kam Hamidieh in twenty eighteen. Twenty-one thousand superconductors, each with a measured critical temperature.

shot.on_screen: Full bibliographic citation card at full width, then a 2x2 stat grid stacked beneath it.
shot.source_tag: Hamidieh 2018, Computational Materials Science 154:346-354 · UCI Superconductivty Data Set

beats.narration_text: Eighty-one features, every one computed from chemical formula alone. Atomic mass. Electron affinity. Thermal conductivity. Valence. No crystal structure. No quantum calculation. Composition only.

shot.on_screen: Feature-family chips card and the accented NOT-IN-THE-TABLE card, stacked full width; exclusions reflow as a wrapping row.
shot.source_tag: Hamidieh 2018 §2 · feature construction from elemental properties

beats.narration_text: Train a gradient-boosted regressor on that table and it predicts critical temperature to roughly nine and a half kelvin error on held-out data. That result is real and reproducible.

shot.on_screen: Reported out-of-sample RMSE at 200px, full width, with three supporting cards stacked beneath.

beats.narration_text: But notice what it learned. It learned to interpolate a table of things we already found.

shot.on_screen: Single accented line reframing the metric as interpolation over known chemistry.
shot.source_tag: Presenter interpretation of the training objective

beats.narration_text: Here is the screening funnel that follows. Score a large candidate space by predicted temperature. Keep the top few hundred. Filter for stability and synthesizability. Out comes a shortlist worth laboratory time.

shot.on_screen: Five funnel rows: label and note in a fixed column, proportional block to the right. Text is never inside a bar.
shot.source_tag: ILLUSTRATIVE SCREENING SCHEMATIC · no discovery campaign was run for this film

beats.narration_text: This schematic is illustrative. I did not run a discovery campaign, and this film claims no new superconductor.

shot.on_screen: Accented illustrative-schematic disclosure beneath the funnel.

beats.narration_text: Here is the limit that matters most. Every genuine breakthrough arrived from outside the distribution. The copper oxides in nineteen eighty-six. The iron pnictides in two thousand eight. A model trained on what we have is weakest at exactly what we want. The compound resembling nothing before it.

shot.on_screen: Inside- and outside-distribution cards stacked top/bottom, then the two dated discoveries stacked.
shot.source_tag: Bednorz & Muller 1986 · Kamihara et al. 2008 · presenter interpretation

beats.narration_text: So what confirms a superconductor? A chain. Theory estimates stability. A chemist synthesizes a sample. A four-probe measurement checks whether resistance truly reaches zero. Magnetic susceptibility tests for the Meissner effect.

shot.on_screen: Five-stage confirmation chain as a VERTICAL stack with down-arrows; only the AI-touched stage is accent.
shot.source_tag: Standard experimental confirmation practice · Meissner & Ochsenfeld 1933

beats.narration_text: AI touches the first box. The remaining steps are physical, slow, and owned by a person.

shot.on_screen: Boundary labels above and below a full-width rule, then the accented Meissner boundary card.

beats.narration_text: Now the case that proves the rubric earns its keep. In July twenty twenty-three, a preprint claimed L K ninety-nine, a copper-doped lead apatite, superconducted at room temperature and ordinary pressure.

shot.on_screen: WHAT WAS CLAIMED panel, full width, upper half of the frame.
shot.source_tag: Lee, Kim et al., arXiv preprints 2307.12008 / 2307.12037 (July 2023)

beats.narration_text: It had an exact composition. It had a dramatic resistivity drop. It failed. Independent groups traced the drop to a copper sulfide impurity changing phase. No Meissner effect was confirmed.

shot.on_screen: WHAT REPLICATION FOUND panel, full width, lower half -- held together with the claim panel for the rest of the scene.
shot.source_tag: Independent replication reports, Aug-Sep 2023 · Cu2S phase-transition explanation

beats.narration_text: Score it on CLAIM. Composition, present. Applicability, unknown. Independent confirmation, failed. Measurement, failed. The verdict sits entirely in the last two axes, and those are precisely the two no model can supply.

shot.on_screen: CLAIM rubric scored against LK-99; each justification sits beneath its axis name so verdict chips keep full width.
shot.source_tag: Presenter framework applied to the 2023 replication record

beats.narration_text: So, can AI discover new quantum materials? It can shrink a search space before anyone enters a laboratory. Genuinely useful. Genuinely bounded. Discovery is the measurement. Run these five questions on the next headline you read.

shot.on_screen: Five-row viewer scaffold with the decision rule, then the centred title close.
shot.source_tag: Presenter CLAIM scaffold · reusable on any AI-materials claim
